assessment: Mizukami et al. investigate the evolutionary origins of coronary arteries in amniotes by comparing vascular morphologies across several species and developmental timepoints. They propose that coronary arteries are a novel structure in amniotes and that they arose from an ancestral vascular network surrounding the outflow tract. The ancestral network is similar to, and may be a remnant of, the transient aortic subepicardial vessels (ASVs) seen in developing mouse and quail hearts.
